correctness.rationale: In the multigroup adaptive SIS dynamics with n=2, B=[[4,1],[1,1/2]], all epidemiological and link rates 1, breaking functions 1 and creation 1 except cr_21(y1)=max(1-2y1,0)^3 (C^2 nonincreasing), the disease-free next-generation radius equals (9+sqrt65)/8>1. Stationarity of y1 forces y1>1/2 if both groups infected; then z21=0 and stationary y2 equation is -y2(3+y2)/4<0. Thus only DFE and y1=1/2,y2=0 partial state exist. Full 6x6 Jacobian eigenvalues {-2 multiplicity3,-1 multiplicity2,-3/4}, independently reconstructed in exact SymPy. For strictly positive creation and positive Q on infection-carrying edges, positive Metzler Perron bound at R0>1, a compact truncated cube, and inward-pointing Brouwer projection ensure nonzero reduced equilibrium; irreducibility plus positive Z propagates any zero coordinate to all, so equilibrium is fully endemic.

Read primary arXiv HTML and checked hypotheses: counterexample has minimum row sum 3/4 and is not refuted by Theorem 5. This is a substantive counterexample to the conjectured implication in its allowed smooth monotone function class plus a meaningful repaired sufficient hypothesis. Resultary papers on static multigroup R0 or other adaptive diseases do not cover the exact mechanism.
